limits: no L05 dispatcher lease or writer token
no approved raw DAT/source archive opened in this run
no SY_* rows or executable config bodies inspected or executed
no legacy database/config write or migration
no product/compiler runtime test or CI
no GitHub mutation or issue closure
objective: Keep legacy configuration write-back disabled until exact source, transaction, concurrency, scope, cache and recovery behavior is proved in a disposable environment.
evidence_basis: The supplemental guide infers that LayoutX.SaveConfig may delete all rows for an FID and then reinsert non-empty configuration.
Transaction boundaries, concurrent-writer handling, complete grammar, current source/build correspondence and cache convergence remain UNKNOWN.
Web publication and immutable pointer rollback do not prove safe legacy DAT/SY_* write-back.

requirements.requirement: Exact approved source/build identity for every read and write consumer is paired with the tested binary.
requirements.sanitized_evidence: source/build manifest identifier, component hashes and mismatch disposition

requirements.requirement: The complete source set for one bounded screen is path-qualified and includes DAT, SY_* rows, FID/variant/PFID, table slots and persisted row identities.
requirements.sanitized_evidence: immutable source-set manifest with counts and hashes; no row values

requirements.requirement: Consumer-specific grammar is verified for LYT, LYS, table slots, empty/null/absent values, encoding and unknown trailing fields.
requirements.sanitized_evidence: grammar version, case identifiers and lossless round-trip digests

requirements.requirement: Executable keys, SQL-like values, hooks and unknown attributes are classified; unsupported content remains quarantined.
requirements.sanitized_evidence: classification totals and allow/deny decision identifiers; no executable bodies

requirements.requirement: Actual delete/reinsert and failure boundaries are observed in a disposable target, including transaction owner and partial-failure state.
requirements.sanitized_evidence: operation stages, transaction outcome, object/count deltas and schema fingerprint

requirements.requirement: Concurrent legacy and Web writers are tested with an expected-state token that rejects stale full-form replacement.
requirements.sanitized_evidence: writer generations, conflict result and unchanged-current proof

requirements.requirement: Authorization and tenant/company/user scope for read, propose, publish and legacy write-back are independently verified.
requirements.sanitized_evidence: synthetic actor/scope classes and allow/deny outcomes

requirements.requirement: A preflight diff uses an explicit object/field allow-list and rejects target, source-set or expected-state drift before mutation.
requirements.sanitized_evidence: diff digest, allow-list version and drift result

requirements.requirement: The target is disposable and proves no production connectivity before any write path is armed.
requirements.sanitized_evidence: opaque target fingerprint, production=false assertion and negative-connect result

requirements.requirement: Lost acknowledgement and partial failure are reconciled from authoritative current rows before any retry; automatic replay is disabled.
requirements.sanitized_evidence: operation identity, authoritative reread digest and retry disposition

requirements.requirement: Legacy Forever1Day cache convergence is measured across clients after commit and rollback; Web invalidation alone is insufficient.
requirements.sanitized_evidence: client generations, refresh/restart method and convergence observations

requirements.requirement: Independent review approves the exact source/build/target head, bounded screen, cleanup and compatibility evidence before a disposable test.
requirements.sanitized_evidence: review identity, exact hashes/head and unresolved findings

adversarial_cases.fault: stale editor saves while another writer has added a row under the same FID
adversarial_cases.expected: expected-state conflict; no delete or partial replacement

adversarial_cases.fault: delete phase succeeds and reinsertion fails
adversarial_cases.expected: transaction behavior is observed; partial state fails acceptance and target is rebuilt

adversarial_cases.fault: duplicate tuple or ambiguous first-row legacy behavior
adversarial_cases.expected: quarantine; never choose an arbitrary winner or add an inferred unique constraint

adversarial_cases.fault: absent, null, empty and explicit zero carry different consumer defaults
adversarial_cases.expected: preserve consumer-specific semantics and raw source identity

adversarial_cases.fault: unknown trailing LYT field or future LYS key is present
adversarial_cases.expected: lossless preservation in evidence and write-back disabled for unsupported grammar

adversarial_cases.fault: workstation-local artifact is newer than the approved shared source
adversarial_cases.expected: timestamp cannot select authority; source remains blocked

adversarial_cases.fault: operation may have committed but acknowledgement is lost
adversarial_cases.expected: authoritative reread by immutable operation identity before retry

adversarial_cases.fault: one WinForms client retains a stale Forever1Day cache
adversarial_cases.expected: cache convergence remains incomplete; do not claim fleet-wide activation

adversarial_cases.fault: rollback candidate references a retired executable key or incompatible schema/build
adversarial_cases.expected: rollback candidate quarantined; current compatible version stays authoritative

adversarial_cases.fault: presentation change attempts to grant capability, widen scope or modify business data
adversarial_cases.expected: deny before mutation and retain authorization/business state unchanged

state_machine.admission_rule: Only a separately authorized controller may admit one bounded nonproduction test after WRB-01..12 are independently verified at the exact head.
state_machine.production_rule: No production or customer database write-back is authorized by this gate.

rollback_boundary: rollback may change a compatible immutable configuration pointer or restore a disposable fixture
rollback never reverses business data or proves transaction rollback from process termination
legacy target cleanup uses rebuild from an authorized snapshot when outcome is uncertain
